title: Clear a snapped piece of filament out of a 3D printer's extruder and leave the extruder ready to load
instruction: A piece of orange filament has snapped off inside the 3D printer's extruder. Take the broken piece out of the extruder and drop it in the grey scrap tray, leave the extruder's tension lever back down where it normally rests, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Labs that build robots and AI hardware print parts around the clock, and filament snapping inside the extruder is a common printer fault. The drive gear and its spring-loaded idler keep gripping the broken piece until the tension lever is held open, so clearing it takes one hand on the lever and the other drawing the piece out.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) The corner of a desktop 3D printer, fixed: a black aluminium 2020 frame beam (20 by 20 mm) along the table 37 cm forward, on two legs; on it a NEMA 17 stepper motor (42 mm cube, black steel) and, in front of it, an aluminium-bodied lever extruder of the common MK8 type for 1.75 mm filament (black housing 4 cm deep, 4.5 cm long left to right, 4 cm tall) 30 cm forward on the centre line. Its filament path, a 2 mm bore, runs left to right 8.5 cm above the table: in through a black inlet fitting on the left, through the nip between a brass MK8 drive gear (40 teeth, 11 mm across, on the motor shaft) and a 623 idler bearing (10 mm across), and out to the right into a white PTFE tube (4 mm outside, 2 mm bore) that runs back and up to the print head on the frame behind (uprights, top beam, bed and screen drawn only); a spool of orange PLA stands on a holder behind on the left. (2) The idler sits under the extruder's red aluminium tension lever (40 g), 1.2 cm from the lever's pivot: an arm 10 cm long from the pivot (1.2 cm left of the centre line) toward the right, ending in a 2.6 cm square ridged pad whose top is 11.6 cm above the table, 8.3 cm right of the centre line. A compression spring under the lever presses the idler onto the filament: with the lever's own weight helping, it takes about 0.85 N at the pad to start the lever moving, 2.5 N to turn it 8 degrees (pad about 1.3 cm down), which lifts the idler off the filament, and 5.1 N at its 20-degree stop. With the lever at rest the gear holds the filament: pulling it 5 mm takes 20 N, and it springs back when let go. (3) A 13 cm piece of standard 1.75 mm orange PLA filament (0.39 g), snapped off inside the extruder: its broken tip 3.5 cm right of the centre line, past the drive gear, and the rest along the path out of the inlet, its outer end 9.5 cm left of the centre line. (4) A grey plastic scrap tray (8 by 20 cm, walls 2.2 cm high) in front, 15 to 23 cm forward, from 5 to 25 cm left of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial, in simulation and in a real trial alike. Out of the extruder: the piece's broken tip has left the inlet (the piece pulled 7.4 cm along the path). In the tray: the piece lying in the scrap tray, both ends inside it. Lever back down: within 4 degrees of its rest (the idler back on the path). 1.0: the piece out of the extruder and in the tray, the lever back down, and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start) at the end; 0.5: the piece out of the extruder at the end; 0.25: the piece pulled at least 3 cm out of the extruder at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the piece still.
reset_notes: Push a fresh 13 cm piece of filament back into the extruder's inlet past the drive gear with the lever held open, let the lever go, and empty the scrap tray.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Real-size printer corner, extruder and 1.75 mm filament (0.39 g). Simplified: the filament is a rigid rod; the gear-and-idler grip is a joint on the filament path with a stiff spring (4000 N/m) that holds the piece while the lever is under 8 degrees and lets it slide once the lever is past 8 degrees or the tip is past the gear; the piece passes through the housing; the printer is fixed. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
